Senses.Explanation: The recurring narrative formula reports that an unnamed monastic asked a question. It opens or advances a public interview; the recorded response may be speech, a shout, another question, or an action. The formula can be introduced by an event frame, as in Zhaozhou Congshen's dog-and-buddha-nature case, or by a biographical transition, as in Tianyi Yihuai's record after he takes up residence. It can name a more specific questioner, as when a Flower Garland lecturer questions Oxhead Zhiwei. Mi'an Xianjie uses the formula while raising the older Baizhang Huaihai exchange in a teaching-hall address, while the Linji Yixuan record uses it to advance separate live interviews. Helin Xuansu, Yunfeng Wenyue, Qingyuan Xingsi, Budai Qici, and Baiyan Fu supply further spoken or acted responses. Those different questions and responses do not create senses of the formula. Zen bends ordinary subject-plus-verb narration into the hinge by which lamp records, recorded sayings, and case collections preserve the questioner's public approach and what a named respondent did next. It is not a genre title or a noun meaning “public interview.”
Senses.Note: The apparatus-clean allowlist count is 27,950 hits across 406 texts. English article choice follows whether the questioner is newly introduced or already present. Item-8 review found one grammatical event formula, not separate event and heading senses: ‘because a monk asked’ (因僧問), ‘there was a monk who asked’ (有僧問), ‘at the time a monk asked’ (時有僧問), ‘after taking up residence, a monk asked’ (住後，僧問), and ‘again raising the case: a monk asked’ (復舉：僧問) all retain the proposition that a monastic asked, even when a compiler uses the formula to open an old case. Every saved questioner is genuinely unnamed. Complete-case review therefore leaves `MasterName` null on all eleven exact-headword rows and names the source, unnamed questioner, and named respondent or later raiser in each note; assigning the respondent would violate the exact-actor rule.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州和尚因僧問。狗子還有佛性。也無。州云無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Gateless Checkpoint (無門關) opens its first case. The record does not name the speaker who asks whether a dog has buddha-nature; Zhaozhou Congshen is the named respondent and answers ‘no.’ All six attribution rungs leave the questioning monk unnamed, so `MasterName` remains null.
